question: What is the network of tiny tubular structures found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Endoplasmic reticulum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** is a complex network of **tiny tubular structures** that are scattered throughout the **cytoplasm** of **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• Electron microscopic studies reveal that the ER divides the **intracellular space** into two distinct compartments: the **luminal** (inside the ER) and the **extra-luminal** (cytoplasm) compartments.
 
• This organelle was first observed by **Keith Porter**, **Albert Claude**, and **Ernest Fullam** in the year **1945**.
 
• The ER is often continuous with the **outer membrane** of the **nucleus** and extends throughout the cell, providing a large **surface area** for various chemical reactions.
 
• It plays a vital role as a **cytoskeletal framework** and acts as a channel for the **transport of materials** between different parts of the cytoplasm or between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Golgi apparatus**:

 
 
• First described by **Camillo Golgi** in **1898**, it consists of flat, disc-shaped sacs called **cisternae** of **0.5μm to 1.0μm** diameter.
 
• Its primary function is the **packaging** and **processing** of proteins and lipids, especially for **secretion**.
 
• It is the site for the formation of **glycoproteins** and **glycolipids**.
 
 
 
• **Lysosome**:
 
 
• These are membrane-bound **vesicular structures** formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
 
• They are rich in almost all types of **hydrolytic enzymes** (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) which are active at an **acidic pH**.
 
• They are often called **suicidal bags** because they can digest the entire cell if it becomes damaged or dead.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:
 
 
• Known as the **powerhouse of the cell**, these double-membrane-bound organelles are responsible for **aerobic respiration**.
 
• They produce cellular energy in the form of **ATP** (Adenosine Triphosphate).
 
• Mitochondria possess their own **DNA** and **70S ribosomes**, making them semi-autonomous organelles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Endoplasmic Reticulum**:

 
 
• **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**: It bears **ribosomes** on its surface. It is actively involved in **protein synthesis** and secretion. It is extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus.
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)**: It lacks **ribosomes**. It is the major site for the synthesis of **lipids** and **steroid hormones**. In animal cells, lipid-like steroid hormones are synthesized in SER.
 
 
 
• **Detoxification**: In the **liver cells** of vertebrates, the SER plays a crucial role in **detoxifying** many poisons and drugs.
 
• **Sarcoplasmic Reticulum**: A specialized type of smooth ER found in **muscle cells** that regulates **calcium ion** concentration, which is essential for muscle contraction.
